channel.title: Sahaj's blog
channel.description: Study notes, AI updates and paper summaries by Sahaj Saliya.

item.title: Deep Learning · LSTM and GRU
item.description: Gated recurrent units: the LSTM's cell state and three gates, the simpler GRU, and an experiment measuring how far gradients reach back through 100 time steps.

item.title: Deep Learning · RNN
item.description: Recurrent networks carry a hidden state across time steps; the unrolled view, nn.RNN shapes, and why gradients vanish over long sequences.

item.title: Deep Learning · CNN intro
item.description: Convolutions as sliding filters with shared weights, padding, stride, pooling, output-size arithmetic, and a small CNN versus an MLP on digits.

item.title: Deep Learning · PyTorch training loop
item.description: The standard PyTorch loop with Dataset, DataLoader, nn.Module, a loss, an optimiser and an evaluation pass, applied to scikit-learn's handwritten digits.

item.title: Deep Learning · PyTorch tensors and autograd
item.description: PyTorch tensors (NumPy-like, with devices and dtypes), the dynamic computation graph, requires_grad, backward(), and no_grad.

item.title: Deep Learning · Dropout
item.description: Dropout randomly zeroes activations during training as a regulariser; inverted scaling, train vs eval behaviour, and its effect on an overfitting MLP.

item.title: Deep Learning · Batch normalisation
item.description: Normalising each feature over the mini-batch, the learnable scale and shift, train vs eval mode, and its effect on a deep MLP.

item.title: Deep Learning · Weight initialisation
item.description: Why initial weight scale matters, Xavier/Glorot for tanh and He/Kaiming for ReLU, and watching activations explode or collapse through 50 layers.

item.title: Deep Learning · Optimisers: SGD, momentum, Adam
item.description: Mini-batch SGD, momentum, RMSProp-style scaling and Adam compared on an ill-conditioned valley, using torch.optim.

item.title: Deep Learning · Activation functions
item.description: Sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, Leaky ReLU and GELU compared by shape and gradient, and why saturating activations make deep networks hard to train.

item.title: Deep Learning · Backpropagation
item.description: Backpropagation as the chain rule applied layer by layer; a two-layer network trained on XOR in pure NumPy, plus a numerical gradient check.

item.title: Deep Learning · Multilayer perceptron
item.description: Adding a hidden layer with a non-linear activation turns the perceptron into an MLP that can solve XOR; a forward pass written in NumPy.

item.title: Deep Learning · The perceptron
item.description: Rosenblatt's perceptron from scratch: a weighted sum, a step function, and the update rule; it learns AND but can never learn XOR.

item.title: Machine Learning · Hyperparameter search
item.description: Tuning with GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV, nested evaluation on a held-out test set, and why random search often wins.

item.title: Machine Learning · Feature engineering
item.description: Creating better inputs: ratios, date parts, binning, interactions, log transforms for skewed values, and target-free encodings.

item.title: Machine Learning · scikit-learn pipelines
item.description: Combining preprocessing and model with Pipeline and ColumnTransformer for mixed numeric and categorical data, so one object is fitted, tuned and saved.

item.title: Machine Learning · Cross-validation
item.description: k-fold, stratified and grouped cross-validation, why one train/test split is noisy, and avoiding leakage by preprocessing inside the folds.

item.title: Machine Learning · Model evaluation metrics
item.description: Confusion matrix, accuracy and why it fails on imbalanced data, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and regression metrics.

item.title: Machine Learning · PCA
item.description: Principal component analysis: rotating data onto directions of maximum variance, explained variance ratio, and compressing the digits dataset.

item.title: Machine Learning · Hierarchical clustering and DBSCAN
item.description: Two alternatives to k-means: agglomerative clustering, which builds a tree of merges, and DBSCAN, which finds dense regions of any shape and labels noise.

item.title: Machine Learning · k-means clustering
item.description: Unsupervised clustering with k-means: the assign/update loop, inertia, choosing k with the elbow and silhouette score.

item.title: Machine Learning · Support vector machines
item.description: SVMs find the widest-margin boundary; support vectors, the C parameter, and the kernel trick for non-linear data.

item.title: Machine Learning · Boosting and XGBoost
item.description: Boosting builds shallow trees one after another, each fixing the previous errors; gradient boosting, learning rate, early stopping, and XGBoost.

item.title: Machine Learning · Random forest
item.description: Bagging many decorrelated trees: bootstrap samples, random feature subsets, out-of-bag score, and feature importances.

item.title: Machine Learning · Decision trees
item.description: How a decision tree chooses splits using Gini impurity, why deep trees overfit, and reading the learned rules.

item.title: Machine Learning · k-nearest neighbours
item.description: k-NN classifies by majority vote of the closest training points; why scaling matters and how k controls the bias–variance trade-off.

item.title: Machine Learning · Regularisation: ridge and lasso
item.description: Overfitting with too many features, and how L2 (ridge) shrinks weights while L1 (lasso) drives some exactly to zero.

item.title: Machine Learning · Logistic regression
item.description: Logistic regression for binary classification: the sigmoid, log-loss, decision thresholds, and predicted probabilities.

item.title: Machine Learning · Gradient descent
item.description: Fitting linear regression by gradient descent from scratch: the gradient of MSE, the learning rate, and what happens when it is too small or too big.

item.title: Machine Learning · Linear regression
item.description: Linear regression with many features: the model, the squared-error cost, the normal equation, and scikit-learn's LinearRegression with RMSE and R².

item.title: Machine Learning · The ML workflow
item.description: The end-to-end supervised learning loop: define the task, split data, pick a baseline, fit, evaluate on held-out data, iterate.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Simple linear regression
item.description: Fitting y = a + bx by least squares, reading slope and intercept, R², residuals, and the bridge to machine learning.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Correlation
item.description: Covariance, Pearson vs Spearman correlation, what r does and doesn't capture, and why correlation is not causation.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · t-test and chi-square
item.description: One-sample, two-sample (Welch) and paired t-tests, and the chi-square test of independence for categorical data.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Hypothesis tests
item.description: The logic of a hypothesis test: null and alternative, test statistic, p-value, significance level, and the two types of error.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Point and interval estimation
item.description: Estimators and their bias, standard error, and building and interpreting 95% confidence intervals with the t distribution.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Sampling
item.description: Population vs sample, simple random vs stratified sampling, sampling bias, and the bootstrap for estimating uncertainty.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Central Limit Theorem
item.description: Why sample means look normal even when the data doesn't, the σ/√n standard error, and a simulation from a skewed distribution.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Continuous distributions
item.description: Uniform, normal and exponential distributions, z-scores, the 68–95–99.7 rule, and computing areas with cdf and ppf.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Discrete distributions
item.description: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric and Poisson distributions: what each one counts, their means, and computing them with scipy.stats.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Random variables
item.description: Random variables as numbers attached to outcomes, PMF vs PDF vs CDF, expectation and variance, and linearity of expectation.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Bayes' theorem
item.description: Bayes' theorem as updating a prior with evidence, the base-rate trap in medical tests, and sequential updating.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Conditional probability
item.description: P(A | B) as shrinking the sample space to B, the multiplication rule, the law of total probability, and the Monty Hall problem by simulation.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Probability rules
item.description: Sample spaces and events, the complement, addition and multiplication rules, independence, and checking them by simulation.

item.title: Probability and Statistics · Descriptive statistics
item.description: Summarising data with centre (mean, median, mode) and spread (variance, standard deviation, IQR), and why the median resists outliers.

item.title: Matplotlib · Mini EDA project
item.description: A small end-to-end exploratory analysis of the Palmer Penguins dataset with pandas and Seaborn: shape, missing values, distributions, groups and relationships.

item.title: Matplotlib · Seaborn statistical plots
item.description: Seaborn on top of Matplotlib: plots driven by DataFrame columns, hue for groups, and the statistical plots (box, violin, regression, heatmap).

item.title: Matplotlib · Styling
item.description: Making plots readable: style sheets, colours, labels with units, annotations, removing chart junk, and saving at the right DPI.

item.title: Matplotlib · Subplots
item.description: Grids of plots with plt.subplots, shared axes, uneven layouts with GridSpec / subplot_mosaic, and constrained layout.

item.title: Matplotlib · Line, bar, scatter and histogram
item.description: The four plots I'll use most and when each fits: line for trends, bar for categories, scatter for relationships, histogram for distributions.

item.title: Matplotlib · Figure and Axes
item.description: Matplotlib's object model: the Figure as the canvas and Axes as one plot, and why the explicit fig, ax = plt.subplots() style is clearer.

item.title: Pandas · Time series
item.description: DatetimeIndex, date_range, the .dt accessor, resampling to weekly or monthly, rolling windows and shift.

item.title: Pandas · pivot_table
item.description: Reshaping between long and wide formats with pivot_table, melt and crosstab, including margins and fill_value.

item.title: Pandas · merge and join
item.description: SQL-style joins with merge (inner, left, right, outer), the indicator flag, validate, and stacking with concat.

item.title: Pandas · groupby
item.description: Split-apply-combine with groupby: aggregations, named agg, multiple keys, transform vs agg, and filter.

item.title: Pandas · Missing data
item.description: Detecting NaN with isna, counting missing values per column, dropna vs fillna, filling with group means, and interpolation.

item.title: Pandas · Cleaning data
item.description: Fixing messy columns: stripping and normalising strings, converting types with to_numeric, renaming, dropping duplicates and mapping categories.

item.title: Pandas · Selection with loc and iloc
item.description: Label-based loc versus position-based iloc, boolean filtering, query(), and avoiding chained assignment.

item.title: Pandas · Reading and writing files
item.description: read_csv and to_csv with the parameters that matter (sep, usecols, dtype, parse_dates, index=False), plus JSON and Parquet.

item.title: Pandas · Series and DataFrame
item.description: Series (a labelled 1-D array) and DataFrame (a table of Series sharing an index), and how index alignment works.
